$comment: MacroScript to MacroDroid mapping. Generated from the MacroDroid LLM Schema v1.0 (MacroDroid 6.0). The 'language' section is hand-written. The command sections are generated.

blockRules: A file holds annotations, then up to four blocks: variables, triggers, constraints and actions.
Each block can occur one time only. Any order is permitted. The recommended order is variables, triggers, constraints, actions.
A macro file must have a triggers block and an actions block.
The variables block and the constraints block are optional.
An action block file (@actionBlock) must not have a triggers block or a constraints block.
No other top-level code is permitted.

comments.doc: /** text */ before a trigger, constraint or action statement. The compiler writes the text to m_comment of that item.

fileRules.identifiers: Letters, digits and underscore. The first character must be a letter or an underscore. Names are case-sensitive.

annotations.name: @description
annotations.description: Sets the macro description. The compiler gives a warning if it is missing.

annotations.name: @enabled
annotations.description: Sets the enabled state after import.

annotations.name: @favourite
annotations.description: Marks the macro as a favourite.

annotations.name: @headingColor
annotations.description: Sets the heading color. Use a color literal, for example #FF2196F3.

annotations.name: @noLog
annotations.description: Stops all logging for the macro.

annotations.name: @actionBlock
annotations.description: Compiles the file as an action block. Triggers and constraints blocks are not permitted.

annotations.name: @disabled
annotations.description: Disables one trigger, constraint or action. Put it before the statement.

annotations.name: @comment
annotations.description: Sets the comment of one item. A /** */ comment does the same thing.

types.valueField: none. A color variable has no initial value. Assign it in the actions block.

declarationModifiers.effect: Refers to a global variable that already exists on the phone. The compiler does not write it to the root globalVariables array. Magic text uses {v=name}.
declarationModifiers.note: Create the global variable on the phone (MacroDroid Variables screen) before you import a macro that uses it. An initial value on a global is a compile error. This rule makes sure that an import never changes a value that is on the phone.

declarationModifiers.effect: Action blocks only. Sets supportsInput true.
Action blocks only. Sets supportsOutput true.

declarationRules: Declare every variable in the variables block before you use it. This includes global variables that are on the phone.
A declaration without a value gets the default: false, 0, empty string, 0.0, empty dict or empty array.
A color variable cannot have an initial value. Write color accent; and then accent = #FF2196F3; in the actions block. An initial value is a compile error.
A global variable cannot have an initial value. An initial value is a compile error.
Local variables compile to macro.localVariables with isLocalVar true. Magic text uses {lv=name}.
Dict and array literals compile to the dictionary field: {"entries": [...], "isArray": false or true}. Array keys are the index as a string: "0", "1", "2".

Each entry is {"key": "k", "variable": {...}}. The variable object has a type field and one value field: StringValue with textValue, IntegerValue with intValue, DecimalValue with decimalValue, BooleanValue with booleanValue.
A nested dict or array is an entry whose variable is {"type": "Dictionary", "entries": [...], "isArray": false or true}. Nesting can go to any depth.

literals.name: duration
literals.rule: Units are ms, s, m and h. You can join units: 1h15m. The compiler converts the value to the unit of the parameter. A plain int is also accepted. A plain int uses the unit of the parameter.

literals.name: color
literals.rule: #RRGGBB gets alpha FF. The compiler writes a signed 32-bit ARGB int. #FFFF0000 becomes -65536.

literals.name: object
literals.rule: Keys can be strings or bare identifiers.

literals.name: constant
literals.rule: Constants are UPPER_CASE. A constant is valid only for the parameter that defines it. You do not import constants.

dayGroups.rule: Day constants are the same everywhere. The compiler puts them in the order that the parameter needs. TimerTrigger and SetAlarmClockAction use Mon first. DayOfWeekConstraint uses Sun first.

interpolation.permittedIn: String literals that go to a parameter with interpolation true, to a string variable, or to a log or notification text.

rules.result: {iterator_dictionary_key} or {iterator_value}. For an array, key gives {iterator_array_index}.
the literal text {battery}. The compiler writes \{battery}, which MacroDroid shows as {battery}.

interpolation.rawMagicText: Text in single braces, for example {battery}, goes to the output with no change, so MacroDroid fills it in. This is an escape hatch. Prefer ${sys.battery}.
errors: Interpolation in a parameter that does not support magic text is a compile error.
${name} where name is not declared and is not a loop alias is a compile error.
interpolation.escapeRule: To show a literal brace, write \{ in MacroScript. The compiler writes \{ only when the text inside the braces is valid magic text (a sys name, v=name or lv=name). In all other cases it writes { with no backslash, because MacroDroid shows a backslash that is not part of an escape.

rules: Each statement is one trigger. Multiple triggers use OR logic: any one starts the macro.
The block must hold at least one trigger. For a macro that you start by hand, write manual(); (EmptyTrigger).
'as label' gives the trigger a name. The compiler gives a labeled trigger a placeholder m_SIGUID (112233445566771, 112233445566772, ...). Use the label in triggeredBy(label).
'when (condition)' adds trigger-level constraints to m_constraintList of that trigger.
Each statement is a condition. All statements must be true (AND).
A statement can use &&, || and ! with parentheses.
If the block has one statement that is a flat OR (a || b || c), the compiler writes a flat list and sets macro.m_isOrCondition true.
Other mixed logic compiles to LogicConstraint items.
Statements run in order. The compiler writes one flat m_actionList.
Braces in if, else and loops become open and close marker actions (IfConditionAction ... EndIfAction, LoopAction ... EndLoopAction).
'when (condition)' after an action call adds action-level constraints to that action only.

statements.compilesTo: One action item with m_classType from the mapping.
The action with m_constraintList set from the condition.

statements.note: Exactly one EndIfAction closes each chain. The condition goes in m_constraintList of the If or ElseIf item.
confirm() must be the whole condition. 'else if (confirm(...))' compiles to ElseIfConfirmedThenAction.

statements.compilesTo: LoopAction m_option 1 (While-Do), condition in m_constraintList, EndLoopAction

statements.note: Put a wait() and a break inside, or the loop runs with no delay.

statements.compilesTo: LoopAction m_option 0, m_fixedOptionVariable from the int variable, EndLoopAction

statements.note: The compiler uses the largest unit that gives a whole number: s=0, m=1, h=2.

statements.compilesTo: IterateDictionaryAction {variableName, isArray from the declaration, dictionaryKeys {keys: []}} ... EndLoopAction
statements.note: key and value are aliases. For a dict: {iterator_dictionary_key} and {iterator_value}. For an array: {iterator_array_index} and {iterator_value}. To walk a nested entry, write for (k, v : d["inner"]); the keys go in dictionaryKeys.
It stops only this run of the macro.
1500ms writes m_delayInSeconds 1 and m_delayInMilliSeconds 500. wait(count, MINUTES) uses a variable: m_variable and unitForVariables.

statements.compilesTo: WaitUntilTriggerAction with the trigger in triggersToWaitFor
statements.note: Give a list for more than one trigger: waitFor([a(), b()]). timeout sets timeoutEnabled true. Named arguments: continueOnTimeout, result (bool variable).

statements.syntax: callBlock("Block Name", inputs: {in1: x}, outputs: {out1: myVar});
statements.note: async: true sets continueActionsWithoutWaiting. The compiler finds the .ms file with @actionBlock and that @name, compiles it into macro.exportedActionBlocks, and uses one placeholder GUID for both.

statements.compilesTo: One item with m_classType ClassName and the given fields, with no checks
statements.note: Use this for a command that the mapping does not have yet. It is permitted in all three blocks.

assignmentRules.json: m_newStringValue "#FF0000" (color variable). This is the only way to give a color variable a value.

assignmentRules.note: Other named arguments: password, passwordToggle, emptyAtStart, showCancel, stopAfterCancel, trueLabel, falseLabel.

assignmentRules.json: dictionaryKeys ["k"] (a plain list of strings), dictionaryOrArrayType 1
assignmentRules.note: dictionaryOrArrayType uses the variable type codes: 0 bool, 1 int, 2 string, 3 decimal. Use -1 when the target is not a dict or array entry. A key can be a variable: d[k] = 5 writes dictionaryKeys ["{lv=k}"].

assignmentNotes: Every assignment writes m_variable as {m_name, m_type, isLocalVar} from the declaration.
Assignment to an undeclared name is a compile error.
Type mismatch is a compile error. Use a cast for dictionary entries: i = (int) d["k"];

conditionRules.json: int: m_intGreaterThan with 4. decimal: LogicConstraint OR of > and ==.
m_stringValue "a", m_stringComparisonType 0, m_stringEqual true, checkCase true
CompareValueConstraint type 4 (dict) or 5 (array), value1 "{lv=d}", value2 "k", comparisonType 6. .containsValue(v) uses 8. With ! in front: 7 and 9.
TriggerThatInvokedConstraint m_siGuidThatInvoked = SIGUID of morning, m_triggerName, m_not false
Any constraint call compiles to that constraint.
a, then LogicConstraint m_option 1 with children b and c

conditionNotes: A condition can use constraint calls, variable comparisons, sys comparisons, triggeredBy() and confirm().
confirm() is valid only as the whole condition of if or else if.
Trigger calls are not valid in a condition. Use the matching constraint. For example use screenOnOff in constraints, not the trigger with the same name.

argumentRules: A command can take one argument with no name. The mapping marks it with positional true. Example: setWifi(TURN_OFF).
Give named arguments in any order.
Leave out an optional argument to use its default.
A required argument with no value is a compile error. An argument with usedWhen is required only when that condition is true.
An unknown argument name is a compile error.
An enum argument also accepts a plain int. Use this only when a constant is missing.

a list of constants, for example [MON, FRI], or a day group. Days of month accept ints: [1, 15]. The compiler writes a bool array of the correct length.

compilerRules: macro.m_GUID is 0. macro.aiGenerated is 1. macro.m_completed is true. These tell MacroDroid to replace placeholder IDs at import.
m_SIGUID is 0 on every item, except items that something references. Those get 11223344556677 followed by a counter: 112233445566771, 112233445566772.
Called action blocks go in macro.exportedActionBlocks. Each block gets a placeholder GUID. ActionBlockAction.actionBlockId uses the same value.
The root globalVariables array is always empty. A global variable must already exist on the phone.
Local variables go in macro.localVariables. Never write m_localVariables.
Every trigger, action and constraint has m_classType and m_SIGUID.
Always write required parameters, also when the value is 0 or false. Leave out optional parameters that hold their default value. Do not write an empty m_constraintList on items.
Always write m_actionList and m_triggerList on the macro, also when they are empty.
Key names and enum values must match the schema exactly. They are case-sensitive.
Escape double quotes and backslashes in every JSON string value.

resolvedQuestions.question: Magic text form for dictionary and array entries
resolvedQuestions.answer: {lv=name[key]} and {v=name[key][sub]}. Keys can hold magic text: {v=Devices[{iterator_array_index}][Name]}.

resolvedQuestions.question: SetVariableAction.dictionaryOrArrayType codes
resolvedQuestions.answer: 0 bool, 1 int, 2 string, 3 decimal, -1 not an entry. The codes are the same as MacroDroidVariableConstraint.dictionaryType.
resolvedQuestions.source: Real exports (0 and 2 seen with boolean and string values) and the schema enum

resolvedQuestions.question: Format of nested dict and array entries
resolvedQuestions.source: Real exports and the schema DictionaryEntry format

resolvedQuestions.question: CompareValueConstraint with dict and array values
resolvedQuestions.answer: type 4 or 5, value1 is the variable as magic text ({lv=d}), comparisonType 6 to 9.
resolvedQuestions.source: Real exports: 44 uses of comparisonType 6 and 7 on arrays

resolvedQuestions.question: Initial value of a color variable
resolvedQuestions.answer: Not permitted. Assign the color in the actions block with SetVariableAction.m_newStringValue, which the schema documents for color variables.

resolvedQuestions.question: Import of global variables that already exist on the phone
resolvedQuestions.answer: The compiler never exports global variables, so an import cannot change them. MacroDroid's own exports of macros that use globals also leave globalVariables empty.

For calendar periods the trigger auto re-arms when the period rolls over (e.g. on the billing day). For rolling windows, cooldownMinutes prevents repeat fires (default = period length). Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.

triggers.name: sensor
triggers.description: Triggers when a value reported by a chosen device sensor crosses a defined threshold. Edge-triggered - fires once when the value crosses the threshold and re-arms only after the value moves back past the threshold. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion and step detector are not. For multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²), useful for orientation-independent movement detection. The value that fired the trigger is available via the [sensor_value] magic text and the name of the sensor via [sensor_type]. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+. Continuous mode pauses in deep sleep; periodic mode samples via alarms and works with the screen off.

params.name: triggerValueMax

params.name: updateMode
params.description: Continuous evaluates every sensor update (higher battery, pauses in deep sleep); Periodic samples once per checkIntervalSeconds via an alarm (works screen-off)

actions.description: Repeat actions a specified number of times, until a condition is met, or for a period of time
notes: Requires matching EndLoopAction. Place all actions to repeat between LoopAction and EndLoopAction. Structure in m_actionList: [LoopAction, ...actions to repeat..., EndLoopAction] Supports fixed count, variable count, while-do, do-while, endless, and timed loops. For polling/retry loops (waiting for an app to close, a variable to change, etc.) either make the state the While-Do condition (m_option=1 with the constraint in m_constraintList) or, in a fixed-count/timed loop, check it each iteration with IfConditionAction + BreakFromLoopAction so the loop exits immediately rather than spinning for the full count/duration. For timed loops (m_option=4), the loop records a start timestamp and exits once the specified duration has elapsed. Magic text {loop_iteration} resolves to the 1-based number of the currently executing iteration of the innermost active loop (any loop type), i.e. 1 on the first pass through to N on the last pass of a loop that runs N times. Resolves to -1 when used outside any loop. The {loop_iteration} magic text option only appears in the magic text picker for actions nested inside a loop/iterator.

actions.name: sensorRead
actions.description: Perform a one-off read of a device sensor and save the result into a variable. Blocks until the sensor is read (or up to 5 seconds). Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion, step detector and heart beat are not. Single-value sensors (light, proximity, pressure, temperature, humidity, step counter, heart rate) save into a decimal variable; multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) save into a dictionary variable with named keys (e.g. x, y, z). The device orientation sensor (type 27) saves value0 = 0 portrait, 1 rotated 90 degrees, 2 upside down, 3 rotated 270 degrees, or -1 when the device is flat; if the driver does not report within 1 second the orientation is derived from the accelerometer. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+ because they require a health permission MacroDroid does not hold - do not use them in macros targeting Android 16+ devices.

params.description: Target variable (MacroDroidVariable object wrapped in m_variable key). Do NOT put m_name/m_type at top level - they must be nested inside m_variable. actions.name: summariseMacros
actions.description: Write a summary of the user's macros and/or action blocks into a dictionary variable. Each entry is keyed by macro name and contains Id, Category, Description, Favourite, Enabled, Last Edited, Last Invoked, Logging allowed, plus Triggers/Actions/Constraints arrays (each with name, configuredName, detail, enabled, constraints). Use this to inspect, count or report on the user's own macros.
notes: Result is a dictionary keyed by macro name. Walk it with IterateDictionaryAction to count or filter; each entry's Triggers/Actions/Constraints are arrays that can themselves be iterated to count items or read each item's name/configuredName/detail.

actions.name: terminateRunning
actions.description: Terminate ONLY the current running instance of this macro (execution stops at this action)
notes: Ends just the invocation that executes it - no subsequent actions in that instance run. It does NOT stop any other running instances of the macro (e.g. a loop started by an earlier invocation keeps running). To stop other running instances - such as an ON/OFF toggle that must stop a running loop - use CancelActiveMacroAction targeting this macro (m_GUID 111) with excludeCurrentInstance true. No serialized parameters.
